$comment: Shared vocabulary every other batch references by name: the glossaries, the funnel-stage
terms, the scope-category terms, and the twelve perspectives. Must run first (see
../_folder_order.json) — the questions batch links its terms into these glossaries, and
survey definitions scope themselves against them.
UNTIL 2026-11-07 the canary was keyed on qualified_name, which for Perspectives is author-controlled
in foundations.md itself (no generated org prefix or version, unlike glossary terms — see
../questions/_batch.json for the contrasting case). It is now a display_name canary; see CANARY CHOICE below.
Perspective type note, kept for the next canary on a Perspective: type 'Perspective' is a subtype of Actor (confirmed with the project owner; both 'Perspective' and
'Actor' resolve it, 'ActorProfile' does not). Recorded because it is genuinely non-obvious:
the type names you would first reach for — GlossaryTerm, ValidValueDefinition, Collection —
all MISS, and a wrong type_name yields a false 'missing' rather than an error. That is the
dangerous failure mode here: a false missing triggers a heal, and a spurious heal of the
survey-definitions batch duplicates step links and takes those definitions out of service.
The bootstrap therefore treats type as optional and matches on qualified_name alone when it
is absent, since qualified_name is globally unique by Egeria convention.
CANARY CHOICE (changed 2026-11-07): the 'Answered At' Scope Category term, matched on display_name as a
GlossaryTerm. It used to be 'Perspective::Admin', the LAST element foundations.md created. The project owner
decided on 2026-11-07 that RE stops creating its own 'Data Owner' and 'Admin' perspectives and uses the content
pack's 'Owner' and 'Administration'. That makes all twelve Perspectives content-pack elements, which Egeria
re-seeds itself, so none of them can say whether THIS document ran: a reset that wiped the glossaries would
still show every Perspective present and the batch would never heal. 'Answered At' is the last element the
document creates that only this document creates. Everything after it is a content-pack Perspective that
exists whether or not the document ran. Verified live on 2026-11-07: exactly one GlossaryTerm has that
display name. Two would read as ambiguous (state unknown, no heal), never as missing.
Keeping 'Perspective::Admin' as the canary would have been actively harmful. Once the coordinator retires that
element, the canary reads missing, the heal re-runs this document, and the heal still cannot make the canary
present, because the document no longer creates it. That repeats until _consecutive_failures stops it.
